title: Put out into the deep (Novo Millennio Ineunte)
hook: John Paul II begins the millennium with duc in altum
tomorrow: why would a pope say faith doesn't start with a rule?

segments.voice: Last week ended on a road. In Redemptor Hominis, the Church's way runs through each real person, by name and face. The line was the person is the way.

Lap pools have a rope where the floor drops away. On one side your feet touch. On the other, they don't. A fisherman named Simon is on the shallow side this morning. He's fished all night on the lake and caught nothing, and he's washing his nets on the shore. A teacher steps into his boat, asks him to push off a little, and teaches the crowd from the water. Then he turns to Simon. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught." Simon is tired. He knows this lake. He knows the night is over. He opens his mouth to answer.
screen: `WHERE THE FLOOR DROPS AWAY.` → `A NIGHT OF EMPTY NETS.` → `LAUNCH OUT INTO THE DEEP.`

segments.voice: His answer is honest. Master, we worked all night and took nothing. But at your word, I'll let down the net. He doesn't pretend the night went well. He goes anyway. And Luke says the nets fill until they start to break. Centuries later, John Paul the Second wrote a letter as the Great Jubilee closed. It's called Novo Millennio Ineunte, at the beginning of the new millennium, and he opens it with this scene, in Latin: duc in altum, put out into the deep. Here's the surprise. A pope at a turning point might be expected to unveil a big new plan. He says the opposite. No formula will save us, he writes; a person will. The program already exists: the Gospel, centered on Christ. So where's the deep water? He names it. Holiness, which he calls the measure of ordinary Christian life, not a prize for a few. And prayer: he asks parishes to become real schools of prayer. The deep isn't some far-off sea. It's the same boat, the same lake, the same nets. Just farther from the shore, at someone else's word.
screen: `AT THY WORD I WILL LET DOWN THE NET.` · `A LETTER AS THE JUBILEE CLOSES.` · `NO NEW PROGRAM: THE GOSPEL.` · `HOLINESS AND PRAYER.` · then, large: `SAME BOAT, DEEPER WATER.`

segments.voice: Choose one part of your inner life that stays near the shore: prayer, scripture, the way you treat one person. Name one stroke farther out, name what usually stops you, and name one plain step for this week. If you pray, you can hand him the empty nets first, the way Simon did.
Put out into the deep. Jesus to a tired fisherman in Luke, and John Paul the Second's word to the Church at a new millennium.
screen: `PUT OUT INTO THE DEEP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: duc in altum. Same boat, same nets, a little farther from the shore. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1597 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHY WOULD A POPE SAY FAITH DOESN'T START WITH A RULE?`

howItsDone: Readers of Novo Millennio Ineunte take its call to holiness and prayer into ordinary parish life, and some parishes and schools take duc in altum as a motto.

chat.meaning: Simon rowed out tired, at someone else's word, in the same boat. John Paul's deep water isn't a new program; it's the same life, farther out.

Redemptor Hominis.meaning: John Paul's letter on Christ, Redeemer of humanity
